The Limits Of Economic Fury

Tom Holland

Gavekal Research | 18 Aug 2026

At the beginning of March, US president Donald Trump said Operation Epic Fury, the US military campaign against Iran, could last “four to five weeks.” Sure enough, what military types refer to as the “kinetic” phase of the war did indeed last five weeks, with the US announcing the suspension of its intense nightly bombing raids against targets in Iran on April 7. But four and a half months after that, with a comprehensive peace no closer in sight, the US administration is now switching its focus to a campaign of “economic fury” in an effort to achieve its strategic aims against Iran.It is not obvious that this latest phase of the conflict is any more likely to result in a quick and easy US victory than the kinetic war. However, the economic implications of a prolonged stand-off may be less ominous than they at first appear. While Iran is not as close to economic collapse as the US administration hopes, the disruption to regional energy trade is not as great as many observers feared.
